title: Parent Functions and Their Key Attributes
domain: Attributes of Functions and Their Inverses
standard_text: 2A.2A graph the functions f(x) = √x, f(x) = 1/x, f(x) = x^3, f(x) = ∛x, f(x) = b^x, f(x) = |x|, and f(x) = log_b(x) where b is 2, 10, and e, and, when applicable, analyze the key attributes such as domain, range, intercepts, symmetries, asymptotic behavior, and maximum and minimum given an interval
meta_desc: Free Algebra II parent functions worksheets for Texas TEKS 2A.2A: domain, range, intercepts, asymptotes, symmetry and maximum and minimum on an interval. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Know each parent function's domain, range, intercepts and asymptotes.
key_sub: 2^x has the asymptote y = 0; log₂ x has the asymptote x = 0.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A parent function is the simplest function of a family: x2, √x, 1x, x3, ∛x, |x|, bx and logb x.
  • Domain: √x needs x ≥ 0, logs need x > 0, 1x needs x ≠ 0.
  • bx has the horizontal asymptote y = 0; logb x has the vertical asymptote x = 0.
  • On an interval, check both ends, and the turning point if it is inside.

Examples

Example

Maximum of f(x) = x2 on −4 ≤ x ≤ 3

f(−4) = 16, f(3) = 9

The minimum is 0 at x = 0

Answer: Maximum 16

Example

Asymptote of f(x) = 2x

2x gets close to 0 on the left

Answer: y = 0

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
All real numbers for √x√x needs x ≥ 0.
Mixing up the asymptotes of 2x and log2 xExponential: y = 0. Log: x = 0.
Checking only one end of the intervalFor x2 on −4 ≤ x ≤ 3, the bigger value is at −4.

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = |x|?
items.e: You can put any real number into |x|. All real numbers.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = x3?
items.e: The graph of x3 keeps going down and up forever, so every y-value is an output. All real numbers.

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = √x?
items.e: You cannot take the square root of a negative number, so √x needs x ≥ 0. x ≥ 0.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = 1x?
items.e: 1x can be any number except 0: a fraction with 1 on top is never 0. y ≠ 0.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = x2?
items.e: The outputs of x2 are never negative, and 0 is an output. y ≥ 0.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = |x|?
items.e: The outputs of |x| are never negative, and 0 is an output. y ≥ 0.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = ex?
items.e: A positive base to any power is positive, so the outputs of ex are always above 0 but never reach 0. y > 0.

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = log x?
items.e: You can only take the logarithm of a positive number, so log x needs x > 0. x > 0.

items.q: Which intercepts does the graph of f(x) = |x| have?
items.e: |x| is 0 when x = 0, so the graph passes through the origin. (0, 0) only.

items.q: Which describes the asymptotes of the graph of f(x) = √x?
items.e: The graph of √x is a smooth curve through (0, 0) that keeps growing: no line it gets closer and closer to. No asymptotes.

items.q: Which intercepts does the graph of f(x) = 2x have?
items.e: Any base to the power 0 is 1, so 2x crosses the y-axis at (0, 1). (0, 1) only.

items.q: Which intercepts does the graph of f(x) = x3 have?
items.e: x3 is 0 when x = 0, so the graph passes through the origin. (0, 0) only.

items.q: Which describes the asymptotes of the graph of f(x) = 10x?
items.e: As x goes far to the left, 10x gets closer and closer to 0: horizontal asymptote y = 0. Horizontal asymptote y = 0 only.

items.q: Which intercepts does the graph of f(x) = log2 x have?
items.e: The log of 1 is 0, so log2 x crosses the x-axis at (1, 0). It never reaches the y-axis. (1, 0) only.

items.q: Which describes the symmetry of the graph of f(x) = 2x?
items.e: The graph of 2x has no mirror line and no point symmetry. Neither.

items.q: Where is f(x) = 1x increasing or decreasing?
c: Decreasing on each part of its domain
items.e: 1x falls on the left of 0 and falls again on the right of 0. Decreasing on each part of its domain.

items.e: As x gets bigger, 2x always gets bigger. Increasing over its whole domain.

items.q: Where is f(x) = |x| increasing or decreasing?
c: Decreasing on each part of its domain
items.e: |x| falls to 0 at x = 0 and then rises. Decreasing for x < 0, increasing for x > 0.

items.q: Which describes the symmetry of the graph of f(x) = x2?
items.e: f(−x) = f(x) for x2: the left side is a mirror image of the right side. Symmetric about the y-axis (even).

items.q: Which describes the symmetry of the graph of f(x) = log x?

items.q: Which describes the symmetry of the graph of f(x) = 1x?
items.e: f(−x) = −f(x) for 1x: turning the graph halfway around the origin gives the same graph. Symmetric about the origin (odd).

sets.title: Maximum and minimum on an interval

items.q: What is the minimum value of f(x) = |x| on the interval −4 ≤ x ≤ 2?
items.e: |x| is smallest at x = 0 (value 0) and largest at the end farthest from 0: f(−4) = 4 and f(2) = 2. The minimum is 0.

items.q: What is the maximum value of f(x) = 2x on the interval 0 ≤ x ≤ 6?
items.e: The function is increasing on this interval: check both ends. f(0) = 1 and f(6) = 64. The maximum is 64.

items.q: What is the maximum value of f(x) = log2 x on the interval 2 ≤ x ≤ 8?
items.e: The function is increasing on this interval: check both ends. f(2) = 1 and f(8) = 3. The maximum is 3.

items.q: What is the maximum value of f(x) = log2 x on the interval 2 ≤ x ≤ 32?
items.e: The function is increasing on this interval: check both ends. f(2) = 1 and f(32) = 5. The maximum is 5.

items.q: What is the maximum value of f(x) = 2x on the interval 0 ≤ x ≤ 7?
items.e: The function is increasing on this interval: check both ends. f(0) = 1 and f(7) = 128. The maximum is 128.

items.q: What is the maximum value of f(x) = log2 x on the interval 32 ≤ x ≤ 128?
items.e: The function is increasing on this interval: check both ends. f(32) = 5 and f(128) = 7. The maximum is 7.

items.q: What is the maximum value of f(x) = x3 on the interval −3 ≤ x ≤ −2?
items.e: The function is increasing on this interval: check both ends. f(−3) = −27 and f(−2) = −8. The maximum is −8.

items.q: What is the minimum value of f(x) = 1x on the interval 3 ≤ x ≤ 4?
items.e: 1x is decreasing for x > 0: the left end gives the maximum 13 and the right end the minimum 14. The minimum is 14.

items.q: What is the minimum value of f(x) = x3 on the interval 1 ≤ x ≤ 3?
items.e: The function is increasing on this interval: check both ends. f(1) = 1 and f(3) = 27. The minimum is 1.

items.q: What is the minimum value of f(x) = |x| on the interval 1 ≤ x ≤ 5?
items.e: There is no turning point inside on this interval: check both ends. f(1) = 1 and f(5) = 5. The minimum is 1.

items.q: What is the maximum value of f(x) = 1x on the interval 2 ≤ x ≤ 6?
items.e: 1x is decreasing for x > 0: the left end gives the maximum 12 and the right end the minimum 16. The maximum is 12.

items.q: What is the minimum value of f(x) = 1x on the interval 3 ≤ x ≤ 6?
items.e: 1x is decreasing for x > 0: the left end gives the maximum 13 and the right end the minimum 16. The minimum is 16.

items.q: What is the minimum value of f(x) = x3 on the interval −3 ≤ x ≤ −1?
items.e: The function is increasing on this interval: check both ends. f(−3) = −27 and f(−1) = −1. The minimum is −27.

items.q: What is the minimum value of f(x) = 1x on the interval 8 ≤ x ≤ 10?
items.e: 1x is decreasing for x > 0: the left end gives the maximum 18 and the right end the minimum 110. The minimum is 110.

items.q: What is the minimum value of f(x) = |x| on the interval −5 ≤ x ≤ −1?
items.e: There is no turning point inside on this interval: check both ends. f(−5) = 5 and f(−1) = 1. The minimum is 1.

items.q: What is the maximum value of f(x) = 1x on the interval 6 ≤ x ≤ 8?
items.e: 1x is decreasing for x > 0: the left end gives the maximum 16 and the right end the minimum 18. The maximum is 16.

items.q: What is the maximum value of f(x) = x3 on the interval −2 ≤ x ≤ 3?
items.e: The function is increasing on this interval: check both ends. f(−2) = −8 and f(3) = 27. The maximum is 27.

items.q: What is the maximum value of f(x) = x2 on the interval −5 ≤ x ≤ 2?
items.e: x2 is smallest at x = 0 (value 0) and largest at the end farthest from 0: f(−5) = 25 and f(2) = 4. The maximum is 25.

items.q: Which parent function has range y ≥ 0 and increases over its whole domain?
items.e: f(x) = √x has domain x ≥ 0, range y ≥ 0, no asymptotes, intercepts (0, 0) only and no symmetry. f(x) = √x.

items.q: Which parent function has domain x ≠ 0 and has no intercepts?
items.e: f(x) = 1x has domain x ≠ 0, range y ≠ 0, asymptotes x = 0 and y = 0, intercepts No intercepts and symmetry about the origin. f(x) = 1x.

items.q: Which parent function has range y > 0 and has only a horizontal asymptote?
items.e: f(x) = ex has domain all real numbers, range y > 0, horizontal asymptote y = 0 only, intercepts (0, 1) only and no symmetry. f(x) = ex.

items.q: Which parent function has range y > 0 and increases over its whole domain?
items.e: f(x) = 2x has domain all real numbers, range y > 0, horizontal asymptote y = 0 only, intercepts (0, 1) only and no symmetry. f(x) = 2x.
